The '''2024–25 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team''' represented [[Texas A&M University]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by sixth-year head coach [[Buzz Williams]] and played their home games at [[Reed Arena]] located in [[College Station, Texas]] as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. They finished the season 23–11, 11–7 in [[2024–25 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in fifth place. They lost in the second round of the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] to [[2024–25 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]], 94–89 in double overtime. They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 4 seed in the South region. They defeated [[2024–25 Yale Bulldogs men's basketball team|Yale]], 80–71, in the first round before losing to [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]], 91–79, in the second round.

On April 1, 2025, head coach Buzz Williams left the team to become the head coach at [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-01 |title=Maryland hires Buzz Williams: Terps poach Texas A&M coach to replace Kevin Willard after controversial exit |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/maryland-hires-buzz-williams-terps-poach-texas-a-m-coach-to-replace-kevin-willard-after-controversial-exit/ |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> On April 4, the school named [[Samford Bulldogs men's basketball|Samford]] head coach [[Bucky McMillan]] the team's new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-05 |title=Texas A&M names McMillan as men's hoops coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44537561/texas-hire-samford-bucky-mcmillan-coach |access-date=2025-10-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2023–24 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Aggies]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 21–15, 9–9 in [[2023–24 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in a tie for seventh place. As the No. 7 seed in the [[2024 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they defeated [[2023–24 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]] and [[2023–24 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] to advance to the semifinals, where they lost to [[2023–24 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]. The Aggies received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]] as a No. 9 seed in the South Region, where they defeated [[2023–24 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]], before falling in overtime to the No 1. seed [[2023–24 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2023-24 Texas A&M Aggies Men's Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/texas-am/men/2024-schedule.html |website=Sports Reference |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Aggies Roll Past Cornhuskers, 98-83, Advance to Second Round |url=https://12thman.com/news/2024/3/22/mens-basketball-aggies-take-lead-into-halftime-against-cornhuskers |website=Texas A&M Athletics |access-date=3 August 2024}}</ref>
